chunks: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated that from ʿAbd al-Aʿla ibn Aʿyan, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who had sexual relations with his wife while he was in iʿtikaf at night during the month of Ramadan. He said: “One expiation is due upon him.”
He said: I said, “Then if he had sexual relations with her during the day?” He said: “Two expiations are due upon him.”

key_terms.الْكَفَّارَةُ: the required expiation for violating a sacred legal restriction
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the month of obligatory fasting
key_terms.كَفَّارَتَانِ: two expiations, indicating compounded liability for two violations
key_terms.لَيْلًا: at night, when fasting restrictions do not apply but iʿtikaf restrictions remain
key_terms.مُعْتَكِفٌ: a person observing iʿtikaf, a spiritual retreat in the mosque
key_terms.نَهَارًا: during the daytime, when the fast of Ramadan is in effect

ai.seo_question: What is the kaffarah for having intercourse while in iʿtikaf during Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who breaks iʿtikaf through sexual intercourse with his wife during Ramadan. It states that intercourse at night requires one kaffarah, while intercourse during the day requires two kaffarahs due to the violation of both iʿtikaf and the Ramadan fast.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.2103 - It is narrated by Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdul-A‘la ibn A‘yan, who said:
"I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a man who engaged in sexual relations with his wife at night while performing i'tikaf during the Month of Ramadan.
Imam (as) said: 'He must pay one expiation.'
I then asked: 'What if he engaged in sexual relations during the day?'
Imam (as) said: 'He must pay two expiations.'"
